frame.caption: The cell: a preset (lib/cells.scad), or "custom" with its diameter and length below
frame.name: CELL

frame.caption: mm, the body's diameter; 0 takes the preset's
frame.name: CELL_D

frame.caption: mm, the body's length, end face to end face; 0 takes the preset's
frame.name: CELL_L

frame.caption: mm, how much bigger the printed grip sees the cell than its diameter: from the coupon set (README)
frame.name: FIT_OFFSET

frame.caption: mm between neighbouring cells' bodies: 0.8, the printed bores just meet
frame.name: CELL_GAP

frame.caption: mm, the cell pitch, overriding diameter + gap (busbars usually set it); 0 takes diameter + gap
frame.name: PITCH

frame.caption: cells across the block
frame.name: NC

frame.caption: cells up the block
frame.name: NR

frame.caption: mm, the printer's build volume, its smallest side: 270 for a Snapmaker U1
frame.name: PRINT_MAX

frame.caption: where the edge cells' bows sit: auto takes the gap where it holds a bow of BOW_SPAN_MIN, else the wall (README, "Grip")
frame.name: GRIP

frame.caption: mm, the bow's span between its roots: the tested length, and the longest drawn
frame.name: BOW_SPAN

frame.caption: mm, the shortest bow drawn: shorter, it is too stiff to spring. Untested below 8
frame.name: BOW_SPAN_MIN

frame.caption: mm, the bow's thickness: two lines of a 0.4 mm nozzle
frame.name: BOW_T

frame.caption: mm on diameter, how far the bows' middles stand inside the cell: flush was a tad loose
frame.name: TIP_PRESS

frame.caption: mm on diameter, the bore round the bows past the cell: a plain bore this size is a bit loose
frame.name: BORE_CLR

frame.caption: mm, the narrowest plastic between two neighbouring pockets: four lines
frame.name: NECK_MIN

frame.caption: mm, an arm between two side neighbours is cut where it narrows to this: thinner won't print as a wall
frame.name: ARM_TIP_W

frame.caption: mm on diameter, the frame's lands to the cell: wider than a spacer's, so a block slides in without binding
frame.name: FRAME_LAND_CLR

frame.caption: mm, about how far apart the wave's lines of contact stand up each cell; their count follows from its length
frame.name: CONTACT_L

frame.caption: mm, a trough's clearance to the cell: the channel the draft rises through
frame.name: CHANNEL

frame.caption: mm, the shortest tie across the wall between two openings one above the other
frame.name: TIE_MIN

frame.caption: the narrowest column between two openings side by side, as a share of the pitch; TIE_MIN at the least
frame.name: COLUMN_SHARE

frame.caption: the least share of the wall between the bands that opens: less, and a short frame opens only in slivers
frame.name: OPEN_MIN

frame.caption: mm, the wall's thickness in the bands: eight lines
frame.name: WALL_T

frame.caption: mm, the outside's bumps behind each cell where it is otherwise plain
frame.name: BIG_AMP

frame.caption: mm, each band of bows along the frame: short, to leave more of the frame to the wave
frame.name: BAND_H

frame.caption: mm, the frame stops this far short of each end face, clear of the terminals and busbars
frame.name: END_CLR
